calls.head: The Predators get in close, the Sharks shoot from distance
calls.body: On shots from in close, Nashville is one of the league’s best, but San Jose is near the bottom. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Predators to do more of their damage around the net.

surprises.head: San Jose hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: San Jose is one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 67 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 127 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

surprises.head: Alex Nedeljkovic stole one
surprises.body: Nedeljkovic allowed 2 goals on 34 shots, worth 4.5 expected goals: 2.5 fewer than expected. That is more than San Jose’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 25 starts.

story.head: Nedeljkovic stands on his head against the Predators
paras: Early in the first, Nicolas Hague and Zack Ostapchuk dropped the gloves, and Mason Marchment opened the scoring for the Sharks. Will Smith stretched the lead to 2-0 early in the third. Ryan O'Reilly pulled the Predators within one on the power play less than five minutes later. With the goalie pulled and just one second left, Steven Stamkos tied it 2-2. Macklin Celebrini scored the only goal of the shootout for the Sharks.

The Predators had a little more of the play and hit two posts and the crossbar, but the Sharks had the finish. Alex Nedeljkovic made 32 saves for the Sharks, and Juuse Saros, who gave up five goals against Vegas in his last start, kept the Preds in it, stopping 30 of 32. The Sharks moved to 4-3-0, fifth in the Pacific, while the Predators fell to 2-2-3, seventh in the Central.
